Coco Gauff ensured the watching American public had something to cheer at the US Open as she progressed to the fourth round on a day when Taylor Fritz, Amanda Anisimova and Madison Keys suffered shock defeats. Gauff, US Open champion in 2023, was facing world No 40 Cristina Bucsa, and though far from her best, did enough to grind out a 6-3 6-4 success to progress to the last 16. The 22-year-old will next face the winner of compatriot Iva Jovic or the Philippines's Alexandra Eala for a quarter-final spot. "I think it was way different playing in the day than at night. Once I was down that break I just told myself I need to accelerate through my shots," Gauff said. messages.text: Allen fight ends in bizarre fashion as Carty falls through ropes in round one

metadata.summary: Dave Allen's heavyweight clash with Thomas Carty at Croke Park ended in a bizarre no contest after the Irish favourite fell out of the ring during the first round.
metadata.content: David Allen fight ends in bizarre fashion as Thomas Carty falls through ropes in round one on Katie Taylor undercard | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content David Allen fight ends in bizarre fashion as Thomas Carty falls through ropes in round one on Katie Taylor undercard Chief support bout for Katie Taylor's farewell fight was over in 82 seconds as Irish favourite, who was expected to win, tumbles through the ropes and is unable to continue; crowd jeered as incident was shown on Croke Park screens Saturday 5 September 2026 23:31, UK Image: Thomas Carty falls through the ropes during the first round of his fight with David Allen Dave Allen's heavyweight clash with Thomas Carty at Croke Park ended in a bizarre no contest after the Irish favourite fell out of the ring during the first round. The chief support for Katie Taylor's final fight before retirement was over after just 82 seconds with Carty - seeking the biggest win of his 12-bout career - unable to continue. Allen caught Carty on the back of the head with a clubbing right hand and the Dublin southpaw tumbled through the ropes as much through momentum as the shot itself and onto the floor, where he was laid on his back. messages.text: Taylor dominates Pili in final fight of career at Croke Park

metadata.summary: Katie Taylor bid an emotional farewell to boxing as the Irish icon dominated Flora Pili in the final fight of her storied career at a packed out Croke Park on Saturday.
metadata.content: Katie Taylor wins final fight of boxing career after beating Flora Pili on emotional night at Dublin's Croke Park | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Katie Taylor wins final fight of boxing career after beating Flora Pili on emotional night at Dublin's Croke Park Katie Taylor beats Flora Pili in the final fight of her boxing career, becoming an undisputed world champion for the third time; the judges score it 100-90, 100-90, 98-91 as Taylor headlines first boxing event at Croke Park since Muhammad Ali fought Al “Blue” Lewis in 1972. Cam Hogwood NFL Journalist @ch_skysports Saturday 5 September 2026 23:39, UK Image: Katie Taylor celebrates her win over Flora Pili at Croke Park Katie Taylor bid an emotional farewell to boxing as the Irish icon dominated Flora Pili in the final fight of her storied career at a packed out Croke Park on Saturday. The 40-year-old stormed to a unanimous decision victory to clinch the vacant WBC super-lightweight belt and bow out as a three-time undisputed world champion with 83,000 fans in attendance at Dublin's historic sporting home. Taylor, an Olympic champion and two-weight undisputed champion, hangs up her gloves widely-recognised as the greatest female boxer in history and a game-changing pioneer for women's sport. It marked the first boxing event to be held at Croke Park since Muhammad Ali fought Al "Blue" Lewis on July 19, 1972.
